main_text.p: & propitium, (quod omnium religionum primum fun-damentum) nam ex Dei inimico amicus & ex peccatore sanctus Dei evadit, & qui Deum habet, omnia habet sibi amica, habet remissionem peccatorum, & qui remissionem peccatorum habet vitam & salutem æternam (inquit Lutherus) & David beatum prædicat, cui non imputat vel remittit Deus peccata, Psal.32. v.2. Quid verè sit illa beatitudo sive felicitas di-sputatione hacce tractante de Remissione peccatorum videbimus, quam in proflictum damus.

Remissio peccatorum (quæ nihil aliud est, quàm pec-cata tegere aut non imputare, Psal.32. v.1. 2. Rom. 4. v.7. 8.) est actio Dei gratuita, quâ propter meritum Christi homini gratis imputatum à spiritu sancto applicatum, sola & verâ fide ap-prehensum fontem & morti æternæ obnoxium, sed verè resipi-scentem à peccato & morte absolvit, ad Dei gloriam & hominis salutem.

Confistit itaquè peccatorum remissio non in radicali peccatorum extirpatione. Rom. 7. v.14. 17. 18. 20. 23. 24. & Gal.5. v.17. 1.Joh.1. v.8. Matth.6. v.12. sed in non imputatione. Psal.32. v.2. Esai.38. v.17. 2.Cor.5. v.19. Ezech.18. v.22. Matth.18. v.27. Pœnarum promeritarum ablatione. Psal.103. v.10. Luc.1. v.77. Rom.8. v.1.

Author tanti beneficii est Jehova, qui solus est judex vitæ & necis, condonans iniquitatem & defectionem & peccatum. Jer.31. v.34. Ego, ego ipse deleo defectiones tuas propter me & peccatorum tuorum non recordor. Esai. 43. v.25. Mich.7. v.18.19. isque solus; Marc.2. v.7. quis potest remit-tere peccata, nisi solus Deus. Luc.5. v.21. Ratio 1. Deus solus est Νομοθέτης, Jac.4. v.12. In quem proprie pec-catur,

page.notes: Small raised mark (asterisk-like sign) after "propitium," at the top of the first line; no matching note printed on this page, so it is not marked in the text. Brace-like mark at the right edge beside "peccatorum" on the 3rd and 4th lines of the first paragraph; a printed mark, not text. "THESIS I.", "II." and "III." are bare or numbered theses and are written as paragraphs, not headings. "Νομοθέτης" is printed with a Latin-looking initial N; I read it as Greek Ν. The faint mirrored text in the middle of the page is show-through and is left out.
